newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Demand seen strong at Portugal's Telecel float.
newsitem.headline: Demand seen strong at Portugal's Telecel float.

text.p: Demand in the flotation of a 35.6 percent stake in Portuguese mobile phone operator Telecel next month will be buoyant as the sector has strong growth potential and the pricing is competitive, analysts said on Thursday.
They said the timing of the sale was favourable as telecoms shares had surged to highs in Portugal.

Telecel competed with only one other mobile phone operator in Portugal, TMN-Telecommunicacoes Moveis Nacionais, a unit of Portugal Telecom (PT), was well-managed and already served much of Portugal's big business, they added.
Telecel said on Wednesday it would offer some 7.6 million shares on the market at between 6,900 and 8,100 escudos per share.
The offer, expected to be completed in Lisbon by December 10, would value Telecel at between 148 and 174 billion escudos ($977 million to $1.15 billion.)
The Telecel shares are expected to be floated on Lisbon bourse, SEAQ in London and the New York stock exchange.
"I think Telecel will be a hot issue," said Daniel Bennett of Lisbon broker M.Valores. "The timing for the sale is good because the telecommunications market is at a high," he added.
Shares in PT, Portugal's dominant telecommunications operator, have surged 48 percent since a first tranche was privatised in June 1995.
PT shares were set to rally in the coming weeks as investors looked forward to a major restructuring in global telecommunications, analysts said.
Analysts forecast strong growth in the market for mobile phones in Portugal in the next few years as economic growth picked up in Europe, creating more disposable income.

One Lisbon-based analyst, who asked not to be identified, said he believed up to 15 percent of Portugal's population of 10 million people could be users of mobile phones by 2000, up from about five percent now.

Mark Howard, analyst with Lloyds Bank Fund Managers in Cascais, said: "Telecel is cheap compared to other big mobile phone operators, such as Italy's Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM) and Britain's Vodafone Group."
He said that if the price to be set in the Telecel flotation were at the lower end of the range, the stage would be set for a rally in the "after market".
Analysts said Telecel could become one of the most liquid stocks on Lisbon bourse. PT's TMN could ultimately be floated too, they added.

The possible licensing of a third mobile phone operator by 1998 was unlikely to have much impact on Telecel's market share in the medium term as the new company struggled for market share against its two established rivals, analysts said.
After the flotation, shareholder AirTouch (Europe) will have 51 percent of Telecel's capital, up from 38.8 percent now.
The stake in Telecel held by Telepri, a holding jointly controlled by Banco Espirito Santo and the Amorim group, will drop from 62.5 percent to 10 percent.
Telecel expects some 66 percent of the offer to be sold directly to institutional investors with the remainder being offered as a public offer to sell on the market.
